newsitem.title: USA: American Disposal increases credit pact.
newsitem.headline: American Disposal increases credit pact.

text.p: American Disposal Services Inc said Wednesday it has completed a credit agreement with its banks increasing the committed amount to $200 million from $125 million.
American Disposal said the amended agreement will reduce its borrowing costs and increase its financial flexibility. The funds will be used for acquisitions and working capital.

The agreement includes ING (U.S.) Capital Corp, as administrative agent, Morgan Guaranty Trust Co of New York, as syndication agent, and Union Bank of California N.A., as documentation agent with Bank of America Illinois and BHF-Bank Aktiengesellschaft as co-agents, it said.
American Disposal also said it has filed a shelf registration statement with the Securities and Exchange Commission for 2.5 million shares of common stock to be used for future acquisitions.

"The combination of our recent successful equity offering which raised $71 million, with this significantly larger credit facility, provides us with the strong financial base and access to capital to continue our growth," said Chief Financial Officer Steve Lavey.

American Disposal provides solid waste collection, transfer and disposal services in Illinois, Indiana, Missouri, Kansas, Oklahoma, Arkansas, Ohio, Pennsylvania, Rhode Island, Massachusetts and Connecticut.
